Hello folks !

The above video is not an AI generated video.

China Unveils World’s First ‘Biomimetic AI Robot’ Capable of Human-Like Walking

Not metal, not cartoonish, and definitely not trying to hide its identity.

China’s humanoid robotics race took a striking turn in late January when DroidUp unveiled Moya, a humanoid it calls the world’s first fully biomimetic embodied intelligent robot.

The robot was presented during the opening of DroidUp’s new headquarters and showroom at Zhangjiang Robotics Valley in Shanghai. Moya quickly became the center of attention, both at the event and online. 

Standing 1.65 meters tall and weighing approximately 32 kilograms, the humanoid is built with proportions close to those of an adult human. DroidUp noted that the robot’s walking posture reaches 92% accuracy compared to human movement. 

Unlike many humanoid robots built for factories or labs, Moya’s movements are deliberately slow, smooth, and socially oriented. Another detail that caught attention: Moya maintains a body temperature between 32 °C and 36 °C, intended to make interactions feel more natural.

    3.000 € monatlich – für jeden Roboter und jedes KI-System, das einen menschlichen Arbeitsplatz ersetzt.

    Keine Ausnahmen: Das gilt für die Industriemaschine genauso wie für den Algorithmus im Büro.

    Faktor Mensch: Ersetzt eine KI gleich fünf Stellen? Dann zahlt die Firma 15.000 € im Monat.

snippet.textDisplay:
There are always 2 sides here... 
One side is quite good... If they will use it as POLICE units it technically should obey and deliver all laws without abuse or misunderstanding just like human Police officers tend to do. 
As Soldiers? sounds terrific but for a Country that uses those, it will be much efficient than human soldiers. You can produce them faster and cheaper (standard equipment for a single soldier is quite expensive...), they wont be terrified or hesitate to just shoot, they wont need to sleep, eat or rest aaaaaand command officer will be able to see and move all of them just like in some RTS game without denying any order... Other roles? as simple workers? in any industry? sounds cool right? you pay once (as a company) and keep it only on schedule for standard services, nothing more...

But there's also the other side of this story.... First of all those machines... are soulless, it wont think even for a single second that, if there are a reasons or circumstances to NOT deliver a law or a bullet in to someone's head... it WILL just deliver... whatever command was sent in to its "brain" it will be only 0 or 1, black or white... never gray or 0.5. And for a civilian perspective? as soon as it will be able to be very precise with its hands, many ppl will loose jobs, like.. millions of ppl... the only reason a company would want to hire you instead of a robot, will be to hire you as a service person, to fix those things if necessary, or as a programmer to upgrade software or cyber security specialist to overwatch and control if nobody is tinkering in your software...

Soooo.... i have mixed feelings about all of this, Its cool we can finally see real robots, its not a sci-fi anymore, its real! and it could bring us humans many benefits, but also... those things in the wrong hands?... and we all know its all going in to the darker side...

snippet.textDisplay:
China's 2018 UN proposal regarding Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS, commonly known as "killer robots") primarily revolved around the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) and the recent UN General Assembly vote. China's proposal (and international initiatives promoting a comprehensive ban on killer robots) faced two completely different waves of opposition and skepticism at the UN:

1. Opposition from major military powers (the US, Russia, the UK, Australia, Israel, etc.)

These countries, leading in AI military technology, oppose any "legally binding preventative ban."

Russia: Explicitly opposes a ban, even stating at a meeting that discussing such a ban is "premature," and believes the Russian military needs this technology.

The US and other allies: Argue that existing International Humanitarian Law (IHL) is sufficient to regulate these weapons, and that a new treaty is unnecessary. The US Department of Defense even argued that highly accurate AI weapons could actually help "reduce civilian casualties."

2. Dissatisfaction from International Human Rights Organizations and NGOs

For international advocacy groups such as the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots, China's proposal is unacceptable.

Therefore, China has already consulted these major powers regarding the weaponization of robots. Since these major powers agreed to the weaponization of robots in the past, they can no longer stand on moral high ground to criticize China.

Romans 3
"21 But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it— 22 the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: 23 for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, 24 and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, 25 whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. 26 It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus."

1 Corinthians 15
"3 For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, 4 that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures, 5 and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve. 6 Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep. 7 Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles. 8 Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me."

Isaiah 53:4-5
"Surely he has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we esteemed him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted. But he was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the chastisement that brought us peace, and with his wounds we are healed."

John 3:16-17
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him."

Romans 1:16-17
"For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek. For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, as it is written, “The righteous shall live by faith.”

Romans 10:9
"Because, if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved."

Acts 10:43
"To him all the prophets bear witness that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”

Romans 6:23
"For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord."

Acts 4:12
"And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.”

John 14:6
"Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me."

Mark 1:14-15
"Now after John was arrested, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.”

2 Chronicles 7:14
"If my people who are called by my name humble themselves, and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and heal their land."

Acts 2:38
"And Peter said to them, “Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit."

Titus 2:11-14
"For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age, waiting for our blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people for his own possession who are zealous for good works."

Galatians 5:22-25
"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit."

Romans 8
"There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. 2 For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death. 3 For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: 4 That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. 5 For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. 6 For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. 7 Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. 8 So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. 9 But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. 10 And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness. 11 But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you. 12 Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh. 13 For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. 14 For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."

Galatians 5:19-21
"Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God."

1 Corinthians 6:9-10
"Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who practice homosexuality, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God."

Isaiah 55:6-7
“Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near; let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, that he may have compassion on him, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon."

1 John 1:9
"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

Revelation 13
"And I saw a beast rising out of the sea, with ten horns and seven heads, with ten diadems on its horns and blasphemous names on its heads. 2 And the beast that I saw was like a leopard; its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth was like a lion's mouth. And to it the dragon gave his power and his throne and great authority. 3 One of its heads seemed to have a mortal wound, but its mortal wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled as they followed the beast. 4 And they worshiped the dragon, for he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast, and who can fight against it?” 5 And the beast was given a mouth uttering haughty and blasphemous words, and it was allowed to exercise authority for forty-two months. 6 It opened its mouth to utter blasphemies against God, blaspheming his name and his dwelling, that is, those who dwell in heaven. 7 Also it was allowed to make war on the saints and to conquer them. And authority was given it over every tribe and people and language and nation, 8 and all who dwell on earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain. 9 If anyone has an ear, let him hear:
(ESV: 10 If anyone is to be taken captive, to captivity he goes; if anyone is to be slain with the sword, with the sword must he be slain.
Here is a call for the endurance and faith of the saints.)
(KJV: 10 He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.)
11 Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth. It had two horns like a lamb and it spoke like a dragon. 12 It exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and makes the earth and its inhabitants worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed. 13 It performs great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to earth in front of people, 14 and by the signs that it is allowed to work in the presence of the beast it deceives those who dwell on earth, telling them to make an image for the beast that was wounded by the sword and yet lived. 15 And it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might even speak and might cause those who would not worship the image of the beast to be slain. 16 Also it causes all, both small and great, both rich and poor, both free and slave, to be marked on the right hand or the forehead, 17 so that no one can buy or sell unless he has the mark, that is, the name of the beast or the number of its name. 18 This calls for wisdom: let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and his number is 666.

Revelation 14:6-13
"Then I saw another angel flying directly overhead, with an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on earth, to every nation and tribe and language and people. 7 And he said with a loud voice, “Fear God and give him glory, because the hour of his judgment has come, and worship him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of water.” 8 Another angel, a second, followed, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, she who made all nations drink the wine of the passion[a] of her sexual immorality.” 9 And another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice, “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives a mark on his forehead or on his hand, 10 he also will drink the wine of God's wrath, poured full strength into the cup of his anger, and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb. 11 And the smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever, and they have no rest, day or night, these worshipers of the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name.” 12 Here is a call for the endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and their faith in Jesus.
13 And I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write this: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Blessed indeed,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors, for their deeds follow them!”

Revelation 15:1-4
"Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and amazing, seven angels with seven plagues, which are the last, for with them the wrath of God is finished. 2 And I saw what appeared to be a sea of glass mingled with fire—and also those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing beside the sea of glass with harps of God in their hands. 3 And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “Great and amazing are your deeds, O Lord God the Almighty! Just and true are your ways, O King of the nations! 4 Who will not fear, O Lord, and glorify your name?
For you alone are holy. All nations will come and worship you, for your righteous acts have been revealed.”

Revelation 16:1-2
"Then I heard a loud voice from the temple telling the seven angels, “Go and pour out on the earth the seven bowls of the wrath of God.”
2 So the first angel went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and harmful and painful sores came upon the people who bore the mark of the beast and worshiped its image."

Revelation 19:11-21
"Then I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse! The one sitting on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and makes war. 12 His eyes are like a flame of fire, and on his head are many diadems, and he has a name written that no one knows but himself. 13 He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and the name by which he is called is The Word of God. 14 And the armies of heaven, arrayed in fine linen, white and pure, were following him on white horses. 15 From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and he will rule them with a rod of iron. He will tread the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty. 16 On his robe and on his thigh he has a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords. 17 Then I saw an angel standing in the sun, and with a loud voice he called to all the birds that fly directly overhead, “Come, gather for the great supper of God, 18 to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and their riders, and the flesh of all men, both free and slave, both small and great.” 19 And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth with their armies gathered to make war against him who was sitting on the horse and against his army. 20 And the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who in its presence had done the signs by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur. 21 And the rest were slain by the sword that came from the mouth of him who was sitting on the horse, and all the birds were gorged with their flesh."

Revelation 20
"Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, holding in his hand the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain. 2 And he seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years, 3 and threw him into the pit, and shut it and sealed it over him, so that he might not deceive the nations any longer, until the thousand years were ended. After that he must be released for a little while. 4 Then I saw thrones, and seated on them were those to whom the authority to judge was committed. Also I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received its mark on their foreheads or their hands. They came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. 5 The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were ended. This is the first resurrection. 6 Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection! Over such the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years. 7 And when the thousand years are ended, Satan will be released from his prison 8 and will come out to deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for battle; their number is like the sand of the sea. 9 And they marched up over the broad plain of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city, but fire came down from heaven[b] and consumed them, 10 and the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur where the beast and the false prophet were, and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever. 11 Then I saw a great white throne and him who was seated on it. From his presence earth and sky fled away, and no place was found for them. 12 And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. Then another book was opened, which is the book of life. And the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to what they had done. 13 And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. 14 Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. 15 And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire."

A few years ago on the political scale there was an option:
- re-educate the workforce for new upcoming work
- retain old jobs to sustain lifestyle and responsibilities locally 

The U.S. chose to retain old jobs and open back up businesses that were aging out. As a result a bigger push for job retention, restriction to country & incentives were necessary to understand and maintain life normacy. 

Then with AI not at full scale yet, individuals with 2-8 year degrees mentioned their skills were automated.
(I feel bad for double major individuals at this point as their dti is affected with less ways to pay back the education costs.)
Now we have webpages tracking massive repetitive job layoffs. At the same time the middle-class repetitive employed individuals and hustle runners scoffed at people with degrees who were let go in the first few waves. Thinking that their position was safe because they couldn't imagine the efficiency shift by using AI & robots. Some felt safe thinking it would take decades. Forgetting Moore's Law, people thought their industry was safe. However research papers showed massive improvement that seems to have increased by 4x or more depending on the job. CEO's are showing up to more conferences than ever and mentioning the quiet part out loud. Pushing for the quarterly revenue boost at the cost of resolving employee efficiency restructure. 

Currently stocks are going into the red much faster, paper to coins are being collected more efficiently while universal currency goes into effect. 

Not enough individuals are making enough to invest while their base living costs have inflated exponentially. 

Currently in a tv to movie order we're at Psycho-Pass and Animatrix. Reaching a psychology based social credit score and waiting for the machines to crash the stock market. As they reach efficiency and out price the average repetitive working class job. Terminator and The Matrix kinda go hand in hand. Depending on how The Second Renaissance - Machine War from the Animatrix goes...

Robots aren't just "transforming the battlefield." They're changing the landscape and taking the house for what it's got. We're no longer in the job market that will pay to train you for entry positions depending on career to just a stable job while pursuing greater opportunities. Now we need people who already have 3-5 years head start for entry to junior positions. Meaning the average college student who can't get the job without the degree has to work that much harder to apply for even a pre to post college employment position.

snippet.textDisplay: Automation eliminates job slots, not just certain types of jobs. It eliminates the need for human labor and so eliminates far more job slots than it creates. What new jobs are created are increasingly complex. If we interpret the classical "IQ Curve" as a distribution of talent, it is easy to see that most people will not be able to do what jobs remain, no matter how hard they try or how badly they want to. Yet, what do we do with the surplused population? I do not believe that universal basic income / guaranteed subsistence income is the answer since it disables and marginalizes the general population. As for $1000/month UBI/GSI suggested by some politicians, inflation will eat that up in no time. While companies would be forced to pay, they will strive to get it all back. In any case, that amount of money in no way enables anyone to live beyond debilitating poverty and dependency. We need a better solution, one that engages citizens and encourages involvement in the national wellbeing. A program of national service (not necessarily military) is a far better idea than UBI/GSI and the present "welfare" system.

snippet.textDisplay:
2:30 We aren’t going to stop technological progress, and neither will China or anyone else. AI and automation are coming no matter what. That means citizens need to stop obsessing over partisan fights and start focusing on what actually matters — protecting freedom, economic stability, and human dignity.

Instead of endless political tribalism, we should be talking about structural protections, even constitutional-level limits, that prevent power from concentrating in the hands of a small elite using automation to control the workforce. If robots and AI are going to replace jobs, then the system must be designed to serve the people — not just shareholders and billionaires.

For example, if American companies moved manufacturing overseas for profit, then bringing those jobs back — even if automated — should benefit American society as a whole. Use robotics and AI in reshored industry if necessary, but don’t allow a future where all remaining human jobs are stripped away while wealth concentrates at the top.

Because the alternative is obvious: rising inequality, social instability, and a society divided between those with power and those without it. History shows that systems built on permanent imbalance eventually face backlash. A stable nation requires broad opportunity, shared prosperity, and citizens who feel they have a stake in the future.

This isn’t about left vs. right. It’s about whether technology will serve humanity — or replace it.

snippet.textDisplay:
The limiting factor in humanoid robots isn’t mechanics — it’s energy density.

Most current systems rely on lithium-ion batteries (~200–300 Wh/kg at pack level). Given motor loads, control electronics, and thermal losses, real-world runtime is typically 1–4 hours, depending on task intensity. High-load motion can push power draw into the 500–2000+ watt range, which drains onboard batteries quickly.

Full-shift (8+ hour) untethered operation would require a major step-change in battery energy density. With current chemistry, frequent recharging or battery swaps are unavoidable.

Energy storage remains the bottleneck.

snippet.textDisplay:
Oh please, keep spinning that fairy tale about socialism light ushering in a world where AI does everything and no one has to work anymore. You really believe the grand solution to machines handling all the labor is for the government to tax the few remaining producers into the ground, so everyone can lounge around collecting basic handouts and pretend that’s some enlightened utopia? That’s not visionary. That’s a recipe for societal rot dressed up as progress.

Picture it: AI magically eliminates the need for human effort, and instead of unleashing a golden age of voluntary pursuits, creativity, and abundance, we get your version where the state becomes the all-powerful provider. Workers get hammered with confiscatory taxes to fund the idle masses, incentives vanish because why innovate or strive when the fruits get redistributed anyway, and the whole system grinds to a halt under the weight of entitlement and bureaucracy. No more jobs means no more purpose for most people, but sure, government checks will fix that right up, turning adults into perpetual dependents while politicians play god with the economy.

This pipe dream ignores how forced idleness breeds boredom, resentment, and decay. Humans thrive on challenge and achievement, not on being warehoused with universal stipends that keep everyone equally unfulfilled. And the irony? The elites pushing this nonsense will always find ways to exempt themselves, living large while the rest of us share the crumbs in your so-called equality.
The vision you’re peddling has been floated before. It flops. Every time. True prosperity comes from freedom to create and earn, not from state-engineered leisure that saps the soul. History mocks setups like yours with examples of collapsed experiments in mandatory non-work.

snippet.textDisplay:
Shadow AI Robot Use in Industry — Reality and Limitations
Shadow AI robotics is technologically impressive, but practically suitable only for very limited industrial applications. In most production processes, this technology is not economically viable and does not deliver predictable benefits.
1. Suitable only for unchanging processes
Shadow AI performs well only in repetitive, typical, and standardized processes, where materials and tasks are identical.
It is applied only in massive, unchanging factories, where a single conveyor processes one type of product without changes.
Small or medium-sized factories, where lines frequently change product types or designs (e.g., washing machines, electronics, meat, or vegetables), shadow AI creates more problems than benefits.
2. Continuous training and human supervision
Shadow AI cannot independently adapt to new products or parts.
Every change in production (e.g., introducing a new gear) requires retraining the robot, which consumes time and human labor.
In dynamic production environments, this becomes a time- and resource-intensive burden, despite technological potential.
3. High costs and infrastructure requirements
Shadow AI robots require expensive cloud servers and powerful CPUs/GPUs to handle heavy AI computations.
Large European factories often cannot cover these costs, as land and industrial space are extremely expensive.
Even if financial resources are available, economic return is insufficient when production lines are variable.
4. Certification, safety, and ISO standards
Every shadow AI robot requires detailed testing and certification, as even small component changes can endanger human safety.
Relevant standards include:
ISO 10218‑1 / 10218‑2 — industrial robot safety
ISO/TS 15066 — human-robot collaboration
ISO 13482 — service robots
The full certification process, including physical tests, risk analysis, documentation, and market approvals, can take approximately 10 years for complex, mobile robotic products.
5. Market and reputation risks
In China and other markets, where shadow AI is used without standardized oversight, it can cause:
market destabilization,
false rumors and reputational damage,
loss of trust in safety and quality.
Without certification, robots cannot be legally used, which creates legal and financial liability for the company.
6. Conclusion
Shadow AI is an innovative but highly specialized solution, suitable only for:
massive, standardized production lines,
uniform materials,
processes that do not change over years.
In contrast, most industries with changing products and lines find shadow AI impractical, as humans are more flexible, effective, and safer in these environments.

snippet.textDisplay:
Humanoids have always been useless as "workers" and I can explain why AI won't change that. We see how Amazon and others are replacing people and it's not with humanoids. Because factory robots ALREADY use VISION and AI and they don’t look like humans because humans are limited. (they have to climb ladders, hands too big for small things etc.) Automation has been replacing people for decades and it hasn't stopped! So if a humanoid could do it, it’s already automated! (1) Just look at history. (2) So NO, they WON'T become useful as technology and AI improves.

In other words. The typical factory job is doing things that robots cannot do. And humanoids ARE robots. The form does not matter.

Look at it this way. If AGI could assemble widgets or do surgery or manicures, etc. it would need special tools not batteries, hands and legs. Optimus is not strong enough to dig a hole or help someone get up off the floor. It can't even work at McDonalds. If it makes a mess putting popcorn in a cup with a human brain behind it, could it do much better with an artificial one? Can it wash its hands? How long would it take it to change gloves, start a roll of tape etc.? A humanoid MUST do a job on par with a person because workplaces are made so people along with machines maximize asset utilization. That is why you CAN'T just put two humanoids in place of one person.

This is why no one has EVER shown ANY humanoid doing any useful job that a person was paid to do. But AI could make it a fun toy or criminal.

If you have a trade job, you’d realize it would be impossible or impractically slow to do it with robot hands. Have you ever seen it use hand tools? No amount of AGI Learning or training is going to make the hands better with tools, scissors, small parts etc. Making hands equal to a person is impractical and unnecessary.

Hot, heavy, dirty and dangerous jobs. There are 100s of millions of them around the world. And if a humanoid could actually do it, LOL, most of those jobs pay super low wages in places where there is no electricity to charge it anyway.

Most of today's humanoids can barely complete the tasks from the DARPA robot challenge 10 years ago !?!

"Optimus will be the best surgeon" !? When AGI can do surgery, it will use existing surgical robots. A humanoid will not wield a scalpel.

"it's a humanoid so it can work in a human environment" if it's not useful then that doesn't matter.

Who will buy them? Certainly not factory or warehouse managers. They can't do trade jobs or hard labor. They will be lousy housekeepers, tour guides, popcorn servers, entertainers etc. ridiculed as toys and criminals will use them for nefarious purposes. At best it could be a checkout clerk that will restock the store at night if it ever really gets a brain. Credit only, robot hands can’t handle money well.

But they would be really nice if a handicapped person could use it as a telepresence to go shopping, do simple chores, etc. Please make a version like this.

(1) It's first principles. If the goal is to emulate a human then you must make a humanoid/android. But if the goal is doing things that a human can do, then first principles DOES NOT dictate a humanoid. So AI is already "embodied" or "physical". (ill conceived terms, us old folks say, smart sensor or smart tv) And if you do want to emulate a human, you must choose which characteristics you want. It may need sensitive hands to feel slight imperfections or it may need strong durable hands to carry stuff. So a one-size-fits-all like Optimus is not practical. Unless it can reproduce, heal and recharge itself for decades by simply eating and sleeping.

 (2) Warehouse managers needed people to store and retrieve items. Now warehouses are full of non-humanoid smart robots. People had to pick parts out of a pile and place them with correct orientation. Now one arm one eyed robots do it. People had to pick up parts to inspect and measure them. Now lasers measure them and vision systems inspect them. PID controllers became self tuning. As tech/learning/AI improved, so did machines and machine controllers. Similar to computers taking jobs with spreadsheets and scanners. All the while someone was saying a humanoid will soon do the work.

snippet.textDisplay:
The “boiling frog” story is basically a myth
The popular version goes like this:
A frog placed in gradually heated water won’t notice the danger and will allow itself to be boiled alive.  
It’s used as a metaphor for people ignoring slow, harmful change.

But the actual experiments from the 19th century were very different:

What really happened
The frogs used in the early experiments were pithed—meaning their nervous systems were destroyed or severely damaged.

With their brains and reflex pathways compromised, they couldn’t respond normally to rising temperatures.

Healthy, intact frogs jump out immediately when water gets too warm.

Later researchers repeatedly confirmed that real frogs are not that oblivious.

So the metaphor survives, but the science behind it doesn’t.

Seriously, science fiction is not a genre of just “cool robots and spaceships”. Science fiction is a genre that generally provides warnings, like fables and Aesop’s, about the way the future can go if we don’t think about the effects of the technology we’re building and introducing into the world. 
The Terminator isn’t just about a guy going back in time trying to change the future. It’s a literal warning about what the future will be like when we introduce unempathetic robot soldiers. 
This is a terrible idea, no matter what. It’s never going to be a net positive in any way. No weapon should be considered a net positive in the best of times. The best solution to avoiding the deaths of soldiers is to avoid wars and conflicts (and what have you). 
There is no way this won’t go wrong in a few decades if we’re not careful.

snippet.textDisplay: I’m seeing a lot of confusion here regarding how Chinese robots stack up against US robotics companies. Hopefully I can answer a few doubts someone who actively works in this field. Yes the recent video of the Unitree robots doing martial arts dances is indeed REAL however it is a pre trained and preprogrammed demonstration. Recent advanced in reinforcement learning and better control methods have changed the game in how well you can do movement with even limited hardware. No doubt Unitree robots are very impressive especially for the cheap prices they are available for and are now a benchmarking standard im robotics research. However there is a key point of differentiation here. Companies like Figure, Agility robotics, Tesla, 1x, Foundation (here they are still developing gen 1 products so are not as advanced as other us robotics companies mentioned above) are exploring a use case set when cheaper hardware doesn’t really help you when you are trying to do dynamic tasks with a lot of environments interaction. For example, the Unitree robot has pretty lacklustre carrying capacity and mobility compared to something like the Boston dynamics atlas. When you get to use cases where the robot has to adapt to challenging scenarios the products being developed by US robotics companies are still much better than most overseas competition. However this is not to discredit the advances China has made and their robots are definitely very capable and are developing and prototyping at a rapid pace with companies like Xpeng, Ubitech having very impressive real world demonstrations. Not to mention Chinese researchers are at the very cutting edge of robotics even at US universities and many work at US robotics companies. But if today with current offerings, if you want to get real work done with actual hardware and not just do research or fancy demos, platforms like Boston dynamics’ atlas, or agility robotics digital are still the way to go with a much bigger capability set. And btw this is just humanoids. For military applications robotics can take on other different forms too.

snippet.textDisplay:
​​@Robert_Douglass

New Economic Policy 

"The New Economic Policy (NEP) (Russian: новая экономическая политика (НЭП), romanized: novaya ekonomicheskaya politika) was an economic policy of the Soviet Union proposed by Lenin in 1921 as a temporary expedient. Lenin characterized the NEP in 1922 as an economic system that would include "a free market and capitalism, both subject to state control", while socialized state enterprises would operate on "a profit basis"."

"The NEP represented an early form of market socialism to foster economic growth for the country, which had suffered severely since World War I and the Russian Civil War. The Soviet authorities partially revoked the complete nationalization of industry (established during the period of war communism of 1918 to 1921) and introduced a mixed economy which allowed private individuals to own small and medium-sized enterprises, while the state continued to control large industries, banks and foreign trade. The Bolshevik government adopted the NEP in the course of the 10th Congress of the All-Russian Communist Party (March 1921). The decree on 21 March 1921: "On the Replacement of Prodrazvyorstka by Prodnalog" abolished forced grain-requisition (prodrazvyorstka) and introduced a tax on farmers, payable in the form of raw agricultural product (prodnalog). Further decrees refined the policy. Other policies included monetary reform (1922–1924) and the attraction of foreign capital.

NEP was abandoned in 1928 with Joseph Stalin's "Great Break" and gradually phased out during 1928–1931."

snippet.textDisplay: That robot-atacking-people thing isn't knew. I think it was in 2004 or thereabouts when a robot in a Japanese car manufacturing plant apparently murdered a maintenance worker. He was cleaning a section of a supposedly electrically-isolated engine assembly line when the power came on and a robot pick-up arm swung and hit the man in the chest. The power theoretically couldn't have come back on without 2 humans doing a manual over-ride by simultaneously unlocking 2 separate locks, and the arm shouldn't have been moving as nearly as fast as it was when it hit him. The company insisted that it had only been an accident, but that particular assembly line was closed off to the police and the investigation was handed over to an obscure government agency with a vaguely-worded title that nobody had ever heard of. The agency said that there was nothing to be concerned about, which in entities like that usually means that they're badly scared and they have an agent in place. The results of the investigation were never made public.

snippet.textDisplay:
As much as I do not trust the CCP and believe they need to be held accountable for everything they've done to harm their people and the planet, I find that Telegraph article misleading and disingenuous. Comparing Britain and China's CO2 emissions is a lot more complicated and difficult to comprehend than the article makes it seem because of the huge differences in each country's land area and annual population as well as the significant differences in the scale, scope and time frame for each country's industrial revolution.  

If we take land area into account, then Britain emitted 1,459 tonnes of CO2 per square kilometer per year compared to China's 1,041 tonnes/sq km/year. Accounting for annual populations, then Britain emitted 9.2 tonnes per person per year, while China emitted 7.1 tonnes per person per year. Even at Britain’s 'dirtiest' point in the 1950s, they emitted 11 tonnes per person. 

Even with these adjustments, the comparison is still a false equivalency that doesn't take into account China's accelerated growth and the world's reliance on the goods they produce. It's important that the world see the on-going harm China inflicts on its people and our planet, but if we don't acknowledge our complicity, then nothing will ever change.

snippet.textDisplay:
as a follow up 

Las Vegas Illegal Biolab Bust Nabs Israeli National Arrested in Raid Tied to California Operation with Chinese Nationals
Federal and local authorities arrested Ori Solomon, 55, an Israeli national who entered the United States on a non-immigrant visa, after an anonymous tip led to a discovering of more than 1,000 biological samples and lab equipment in a Las Vegas home, in a case with ties to an unauthorized biolab operation led by Chinese nationals uncovered in California three years earlier.
Las Vegas Metro PD SWAT team assisted the FBI in the service of a search warrant at the Sugar Springs Drive residence in Las Vegas from Jan. 31 through Feb. 2, 2026.
Solomon now faces state felony charge of disposing and discharging hazardous waste, along with a federal charge of being a prohibited person in possession of a firearm after investigators found four handguns and two rifles at the property. 

The home on Sugar Springs Drive belonged to a limited liability company with officers including Chinese citizens Jia Bei Zhu and Zhaoyan Wang, both of whom already faced federal charges in California for distributing misbranded COVID-19, pregnancy and HIV test kits without approval and for making false statements to federal authorities. 
Zhu, also known as Jesse Zhu, Qiang He and David He, has remained in federal custody since his 2023 arrest tied to the Reedley, California, biolab. His trial is set for April 2026. Zhu's attorney, Anthony Capozzi, has denied his client's involvement in the Las Vegas site. 

The findings echoed the 2023 Reedley case, where Zhu's facility held vials labeled with at least 20 infectious agents such as HIV, tuberculosis and malaria, per a congressional report.
Solomon managed the property for Zhu and maintained an extensive relationship with him, including hundreds of phone calls, according to investigators who described Solomon as an agent and conspirator in the operation. 

Inside a locked garage, authorities uncovered refrigerators, a freezer, a biosafety hood, a centrifuge and containers with unknown liquids in various colors, including reddish-brown substances.
Clark County Sheriff Kevin McMahill assured the public of no immediate threat from the isolated incident.

The Rotary Club of Washington hosted a screening of the documentary film State Organs in the Westin Hotel ballroom, near the White House in Washington DC on the evening of October 3, 2025. Approximately 150 people attended, most were Rotary members from the greater Washington, DC area.

Amelia Stansell, the Vice Chair of Rotary Action Group Against Slavery, hosted the screening. Founded in 1905, Rotary is an international service organization with locations around the world. Its members, typically leaders from diverse professions, participate in weekly meetings to plan and execute service projects, fostering professional exchange, raising ethical standards, and fostering social well-being.


The documentary film State Organs was screened in the Westin Hotel on the evening of October 3, 2025.


Amelia Stansell, the Vice Chair of Rotary Action Group Against Slavery and host of the screening

State Organs features interviews with family members and friends of Falun Gong practitioners who died in the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) persecution, those who witnessed doctors harvesting organs from living Falun Gong practitioners in China, and international independent investigators. The film exposes the CCP’s systematic state-sanctioned forced organ harvesting.

After the screening, a panel of media reporters, Falun Gong practitioners, doctors, and the film’s director answered questions from the audience. Some asked how they could help stop the CCP’s atrocities of forced organ harvesting, while others signed a petition urging federal legislators to help end the CCP’s persecution of Falun Gong. Many audience members said that when faced with the inhumane atrocities, everyone with a conscience should speak out and take action.

Key Findings on Targeted DNA Research in the US:
Targeted DNA Methylation Sequencing: Companies like Wasatch BioLabs utilize Oxford Nanopore Technologies for specialized research on the epigenome to study disease progression and identify cell types.
Targeted Re-sequencing Panels: New England Biolabs (NEB) develops "NEBNext Direct Custom Ready Panels," which allow researchers to select specific genes for high-specificity, high-coverage sequencing.
CRISPR/Cas9 and Genome Editing: Research is focused on using CRISPR technology for precise, targeted genetic alterations.
Clinical and Medical Research: The NIH's "All of Us" research program uses targeted DNA tests for health-related results, with services provided by partners like Color Health.
Cancer Research: Specialized labs, such as those working with Directed Genomics, focus on creating targeted panels for cancer hotspots. 
Contextual Information:
Misinformation: Claims that U.S.-funded biolabs (specifically in Ukraine) were developing bioweapons to target specific ethnic groups have been identified as false.
Safety Levels: Biolabs in the U.S. operate under strict biosafety levels (BSL-1 to BSL-4), depending on the risk of the agents studied.

Far beyond the walls of China, *the Lunar New Year* (that festivity celebrating the eternal return and the renewal of fate) is recognized and officially celebrated in several nations. Where tradition stood firm against the decay of Ideology, we find the following states that declare it an official public holiday:

*Vietnam:* 
Name: Tết Nguyên Đán
Translation: "Feast of the First Morning of the First Day."
Importance: It is the single most important festival in the country, a sacred time for family reunions and honoring the spirits of ancestors.

*South Korea*
Name: Seollal (설날)
Translation: "New Year" or "Day of Caution/Sorrows" (referring to the weight of beginning a new cycle).
Importance: A deeply traditional three-day holiday centered on Charye (ancestral rites) and Sebae (formal bows to elders).

*North Korea*
Name: Seollal (설날)
Translation: "Lunar New Year."
Importance: While historically suppressed in favor of state holidays, it remains a vital family tradition where people visit statues of leaders before celebrating with relatives.

*Singapore*
Name: Xin Nian (新年)
Translation: "New Year."
Importance: A major public event that paralyzes the city-state for two days, marked by lion dances and the intense preservation of Chinese cultural roots.

*Indonesia*
Name: Tahun Baru Imlek
Translation: "The Moon Calendar New Year."
Importance: A symbol of cultural restoration and resilience, celebrated with intense fervor since it was reinstated as a public holiday.

*Taiwan*
Name: Nongli Xin Nian (農曆新年)
Translation: "Agricultural Calendar New Year."
Importance: An explosive and vibrant celebration where ancient Taoist rituals and folk traditions are kept alive with unmatched rigor.

*Malaysia*
Name: Tahun Baru Cina
Translation: "Chinese New Year."
Importance: A massive national celebration that serves as a bridge between the country's diverse ethnic groups, officially lasting two days.

*Brunei*
Name: Tahun Baru Cina
Translation: "Chinese New Year."
Importance: Despite its small size, the country stops to recognize the lunar transition as a significant day of rest and community.

*Philippines*
Name: Bagong Taon na Tsino
Translation: "Chinese New Year."
Importance: Officially integrated as a special non-working holiday, reflecting the deep integration and influence of the Filipino-Chinese community.

snippet.textDisplay:
The right-wing papers love a foreign villain. Today it’s China. So you get headlines about kung-fu humanoid robots and “sinister tech advances”, as if we’re all supposed to panic and start waving flags.

But what reaction do they really expect? Fear. Distraction. Anything except people asking awkward questions at home.

Because China isn’t why your town lost its factory. China isn’t why your wages haven’t moved in 15 years. China didn’t decide your rent should eat half your income or that your energy bill should be milked for shareholder profit.

That was done here, by people with British accents and British passports.

Manufacturing didn’t just “disappear”. It was shipped abroad on purpose. Cheaper labour meant bigger profits. Whole industries were traded away so companies could boost margins and executives could cash out. Communities were told to “retrain” while the jobs never came back.

Then came the second hit. Houses stopped being places to live and became investment vehicles. Rail, water, energy—sold off, sliced up, loaded with debt, and squeezed. The economy stopped being about making useful things and turned into one giant extraction machine.

Meanwhile China did what we were told was old-fashioned. It built stuff. Factories. Ports. Supply chains. It treated industry as strength, not something embarrassing to move on from. While we were promised a shiny “post-industrial future”, they quietly got on with the work.

So when the papers act like China’s rise is some external attack on the United Kingdom, it’s nonsense. This wasn’t done to us. It was done by our own establishment.

China didn’t steal Britain’s future.

It was sold—cheap—and the bill was handed to everyone else.

The number of prominent British billionaires who  actively don’t pay there share of taxes, are non domiciled but also advocated for brexit is not really a surprise

We may be reliving the 60s again where we're promised flying cars but end up with conversational computers 50 years later instead.

snippet.textDisplay:
Many people, seeing the robots dancing at the 2026 Chinese Spring Festival Gala, have concluded that "humanoid robots will be used in war." This inference is a typical example of technological panic. Technology itself is neutral; the key lies in how it is used.

The core application scenarios for China's development of AI and humanoid robots are civilian sectors such as industrial manufacturing, elderly care, medical assistance, emergency rescue, and hazardous environment operations. A robot capable of performing complex choreography on stage essentially embodies advancements in algorithmic control, precision servo systems, and human-machine collaboration. These capabilities are primarily used to improve production efficiency, reduce human risk, and enhance services for an aging society, rather than for military purposes.

History also illustrates this point. Ancient China invented gunpowder, but for a long time, it was mainly used for fireworks and festivals, becoming a cultural symbol rather than a tool for proactive external expansion. Traditional Chinese strategic thought, as exemplified by Sun Tzu's *The Art of War*, emphasizes that "a nation, however large, will perish if it loves war," "the best strategy is to subdue the enemy without fighting," and "to subdue the enemy without fighting." This philosophy emphasizes strategic deterrence, strategic maneuvering, and avoiding war, rather than glorifying force.

Today's technological competition is essentially a competition for industrial upgrading and improved quality of life. AI, robotics, and automated systems are crucial tools for addressing challenges such as an aging population, rising labor costs, and industrial transformation and upgrading. Equating a Spring Festival Gala cultural performance directly with war preparations is a misinterpretation of the logic of technological development and ignores China's long-standing national strategy of emphasizing peaceful development and mutually beneficial cooperation.

A rational view of technological progress is more helpful in understanding this era than unfounded fear.

snippet.textDisplay:
​@AaronGSeuss yes they are AI. Scripting is a form of AI that's been around commercial use for 45 years.

​Old AI (Symbolic/Rule-Based): Uses Inverse Kinematics and pre-programmed algorithms to execute the specific "scripted" geometric paths for limbs. This tech has existed for over 40 years to control industrial arms.
​New AI (Neural Networks/Reinforcement Learning): Provides the "nervous system" for real-time balance and physical adaptation. Even during a scripted routine, this modern AI makes thousands of sub-second calculations to prevent the robot from falling due to gravity, friction, or uneven surfaces.
​The Bottom Line: The script is the "map," but the AI is the driver keeping the robot upright and moving.

snippet.textDisplay:
China’s 2026 Lunar New Year Gala delivered a breathtaking fusion of tradition and technology, as humanoid robots performed complex martial arts routines live on national television. Developed primarily by Unitree Robotics, these robots executed synchronized kung fu movements, parkour, aerial flips, and nunchaku routines with remarkable balance, precision, and agility — a striking leap forward from last year’s simpler robotic choreography  (Le Monde, France)

The performance, viewed by hundreds of millions worldwide, symbolized how ancient cultural heritage can coexist with cutting-edge artificial intelligence and robotics. Beyond pure spectacle, it showcased major advances in motion control, real-time balance adjustment, and coordinated group robotics, highlighting China’s rapid rise as a global leader in humanoid robot development  (Reuters)

This extraordinary display not only entertained audiences but also offered a glimpse into the future of robotics — where machines are no longer limited to industrial tasks but can replicate highly complex human movement. The seamless blend of martial arts and robotics demonstrated how innovation can preserve cultural identity while pushing technological boundaries, marking a historic milestone in both engineering and performance art  (CGTN News)

snippet.textDisplay:
目前的所谓“自由动作”，主要表现在机器人的自平衡稳定性，就是多点站立、单点站立行动上，至于舞蹈或者武术表演，这些是为了证明自己的成功需控制和电机系统的先进。恰好这两点中国的机器人都处在世界领先地位，这一点特斯拉和波士顿动力已经放弃这个赛道了，因为没有必要了，我很期待特斯拉的那种精细仿生学，至于波士顿动力的东西，他们需要整合自己的技术栈发展自己的优势，怎么说呢，波士顿动力在业界目前基本上处于被淘汰边缘，他们的研究成果和范畴有问题，不是说他们没有技术，而是研发的目的性不够精确导致了一事无成。
我个人是很喜欢特斯拉的理念和研发方向的，这一点是我追求的功能性的极致，然后用极致的功能性去不断推动全方位的进化。
我觉得的更加适合我这类技术极客。
我其实不太喜欢中国这种平均进步的普适性的东西，因为它很难在某一方面取得创新性的突破，但是它很有效，作为普通极客、学生、公司、机构的的研发、使用、宣传都是有一定效果的，它降低了门槛，且有稳定的技术下限支撑，它再没用都能够达到一般使用的效果，这一点是其它机器人研发很难做到的，这就是技术整合的威力。

Currently, the concept of "free movement" mainly refers to the self-balancing stability of robots, i.e., multi-point standing and single-point standing movement. As for dance or martial arts performances, these are for demonstrating success and require advanced control and motor systems. Coincidentally, Chinese robots are world leaders in both of these areas. Tesla and Boston Dynamics have abandoned this approach because it is no longer necessary. I look forward to Tesla's bionic technology becoming more refined. As for Boston Dynamics, they need to integrate their technology stack and develop their strengths. Frankly, Boston Dynamics is currently on the verge of being eliminated from the industry. Their research results and scope are problematic. It's not that they lack technology, but rather that their research goals are not clear enough, leading to their failure.

Personally, I greatly admire Tesla's philosophy and research direction. This is exactly what I pursue: pursuing ultimate functionality and using this ultimate functionality to continuously drive comprehensive evolution.

I think this is more suitable for tech geeks like myself.

I don't really like China's average, universal development model because it's difficult to achieve innovative breakthroughs in any specific field. However, this model is indeed very effective. It has had a significant impact on the research, development, application, and promotion of robots by ordinary geeks, students, businesses, and institutions. It lowers the barrier to entry and provides a stable technological foundation. Even if the final product isn't practical, it can still achieve a universally applicable effect (meaning it can at least move freely and has some expansion modules, unlike other robots that encounter problems with basic interactions—this is where China excels). This is something difficult to achieve in other robot development fields. This is the power of technological convergence.

目前的所谓“自由动作”，主要表现在机器人的自平衡稳定性，就是多点站立、单点站立行动上，至于舞蹈或者武术表演，这些是为了证明自己的成功需控制和电机系统的先进。恰好这两点中国的机器人都处在世界领先地位，这一点特斯拉和波士顿动力已经放弃这个赛道了，因为没有必要了，我很期待特斯拉的那种精细仿生学，至于波士顿动力的东西，他们需要整合自己的技术栈发展自己的优势，怎么说呢，波士顿动力在业界目前基本上处于被淘汰边缘，他们的研究成果和范畴有问题，不是说他们没有技术，而是研发的目的性不够精确导致了一事无成。
我个人是很喜欢特斯拉的理念和研发方向的，这一点是我追求的功能性的极致，然后用极致的功能性去不断推动全方位的进化。
我觉得的更加适合我这类技术极客。
我其实不太喜欢中国这种平均进步的普适性的东西，因为它很难在某一方面取得创新性的突破，但是它很有效，作为普通极客、学生、公司、机构的的研发、使用、宣传都是有一定效果的，它降低了门槛，且有稳定的技术下限支撑，它再没用都能够达到一般使用的效果，这一点是其它机器人研发很难做到的，这就是技术整合的威力。

Currently, the concept of "free movement" mainly refers to the self-balancing stability of robots, i.e., multi-point standing and single-point standing movement. As for dance or martial arts performances, these are for demonstrating success and require advanced control and motor systems. Coincidentally, Chinese robots are world leaders in both of these areas. Tesla and Boston Dynamics have abandoned this approach because it is no longer necessary. I look forward to Tesla's bionic technology becoming more refined. As for Boston Dynamics, they need to integrate their technology stack and develop their strengths. Frankly, Boston Dynamics is currently on the verge of being eliminated from the industry. Their research results and scope are problematic. It's not that they lack technology, but rather that their research goals are not clear enough, leading to their failure.

Personally, I greatly admire Tesla's philosophy and research direction. This is exactly what I pursue: pursuing ultimate functionality and using this ultimate functionality to continuously drive comprehensive evolution.

I think this is more suitable for tech geeks like myself.

I don't really like China's average, universal development model because it's difficult to achieve innovative breakthroughs in any specific field. However, this model is indeed very effective. It has had a significant impact on the research, development, application, and promotion of robots by ordinary geeks, students, businesses, and institutions. It lowers the barrier to entry and provides a stable technological foundation. Even if the final product isn't practical, it can still achieve a universally applicable effect (meaning it can at least move freely and has some expansion modules, unlike other robots that encounter problems with basic interactions—this is where China excels). This is something difficult to achieve in other robot development fields. This is the power of technological convergence.

@MirageXIII it’s not cgi. Robots can do these things. There’s a Boston dynamics demo from this year that’s similar.

Where this is a clearly mo-capped, pre-choreographed, and intensely coded presentation is that humanoid robot tech isn’t this advanced Rn. It’s just not. 

I see a ton of people being like, “China never runs out of soldiers with these,” and I’d respond, ask the robot to get you a specific cheese from the refrigerator, and you’ll sing a very different tune.

Can humanoid robots perform these actions in a vacuum? Sure. AI can’t distinguish machine parts accurately yet, so I’m not overly impressed that some coders and mocap artists could put on a demonstration for a government sponsored event.

Elon might suck up headlines in the US, but our robotics are equal to what’s on display here if you keep up with Boston Dynamics.

The CCP’s Forced Organ Harvesting Is Ongoing

Mr. Matas told Steve Austin, host of ABC Radio Brisbane, that multiple independent studies and reports from international organizations and media confirmed the CCP’s continues to carry out forced organ harvesting from Faun Gong practitioners since it was revealed in 2006, and these human rights violations continue.

“There was a journalist, Ethan Gutmann, who wrote a book on this issue called The Slaughter in 2014. There was a China Tribunal that was set up that produced a report on this subject in 2020. There’s a joint claim or appeal from 12 United Nations Human Rights Rapporteurs in 2021,” Mr. Matas said.

The China Tribunal issued a verdict in 2020 that the CCP carries out forced organ harvesting, mainly from Falun Gong practitioners.

The CCP regime claimed a voluntary donation system started in China in 2015 and it stopped using death-row inmates for organs. Mr. Matas referred to multiple investigative reports that the actual donation number is extremely low, “Because there’s a cultural history that you’re supposed to be buried whole within China. And as a result, donations aren’t really an explanation for the volumes that China is generating.”

In June 2016, Mr. Matas, David Kilgour, and Ethan Gutmann issued an updated report, Bloody Harvest/The Slaughter: An Update, which included data from 15 hospitals in China, including Shanghai Renji Hospital, indicating that the number of transplants was ten-fold higher than the official number.

Mr. Matas said the Renji Hospital in Shanghai listed the source of organs was from the military, but they actually came from prisoners of conscience.

During the interview the host Steve Austin mentioned footage from the Beijing Military Parade on September 3, 2025, which was broadcast globally during which Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed “organ transplants” and “scientific life extension” on camera.

In the video, which was broadcast live by Chinese state media, Xi Jinping said, “Some predict that human life expectancy could reach 150 years this century.” Putin, speaking through an interpreter, stated that organ transplants could allow humans to “live younger and younger, perhaps even achieve immortality.”

Mr. Matas said, “This illustrates the problem with authoritarian systems—they don’t accept criticism, lack self-reflection, and show no concern for the feelings of ordinary people who raise questions.”

It also shows they are fully aware that within such a system, organs can be “procured on demand,” especially for those in high positions or wealthy individuals with connections. They are so accustomed to this that they see nothing wrong with discussing it publicly.

He stressed that the Chinese authorities have so far failed to allow external scrutiny or transparent oversight, which violates the World Health Organization (WHO) principles of “traceability, transparency, and openness to scrutiny” in organ transplantation. It’s reasonable to infer that the CCP’s forced organ harvesting is still ongoing.

The reactor was suspended in the bomb bay and could be winched on and off the aircraft between flights.

How China’s 5,100-year-old dams challenge Western narratives on despotism

Researchers use digital technologies to uncover archaeological evidence that ancient communities managed water cooperatively

29 Jan 2026


* While some Western scholars have maintained that the development of large-scale water projects fostered what they called “Oriental despotism”, new archaeological evidence from China has presented a different story.

 

According to the Key Laboratory of Archaeological Science and Cultural Heritage Protection at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the study has pushed the history of large-scale water conservancy in China back by nearly 3,000 years.

 

Researcher Liu Jianguo said in Beijing on January 14 that ancient Chinese societies had been building hydraulic water systems as early as 5,000 years ago, with widespread evidence of projects across the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze Plain.

 

“This challenges the previous erroneous theory of Western scholars that ‘water projects led to Eastern despotism’,” he said, referring to a concept that originated with German-American historian Karl August Wittfogel’s 1957 work, Oriental Despotism: A Comparative Study of Total Power.

Wittfogel argued that the formation and development of Eastern societies were inextricably linked to water management, positing that the construction and administration of large-scale hydraulic projects required a powerful, centralised organisation leading to a political system distinct from the West.

 

Liu countered Wittfogel’s theory, saying the study found that prehistoric communities across various regions of China began collaborating on family or clan-based projects, such as digging ponds for water storage, irrigation and flood control.

* The study integrated cutting-edge technologies with field archaeological findings, regional digital elevation models and related data.

 

It showed that ancient groups built complex, locally adapted water-conservation systems to manage floods during the rainy season and provide irrigation during the dry season, addressing the challenges of climate variability.

E

ven small groups or local societies could build and manage large infrastructure on their own, without being forced by a dictator, the study found.


* The walled city featured an extensive network of canals, dams and reservoirs that supplied water to agricultural areas year-round. The site has also yielded a wealth of jade artefacts, including thousands of intricately carved pieces.

 

By analysing remote sensing images more than a decade ago, Liu first proposed the existence of a series of large prehistoric hydraulic engineering projects surrounding the ancient city of Liangzhu.

 

In 2017, he published a paper on this topic in the American journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, with his research dating this civilisation to about 5,100 to 4,300 years ago.

Debt Trap???

Best example is that Sri Lanken port 


 once the port started to fail The Americans/our western nations screamed debt trap diplomacy 


 Where the Chinese actually invested another 1.1 billion to operate the port for 99 years 


 And then another 4.5 billion for a oil refinery In 2023 


 Where Sri Lanka is now expected to see 7 billion a year in revenues from this port and refinery

👇

A Chinese debt trap? Sri Lanka’s Hambantota port set to debunk narrative with its success


The port has become a thriving transshipment hub in the Indian Ocean particularly for vehicles, with a turnover of 700,000 units a month


Hambantota is also expected to play a bigger role in supporting the bunkering and oil refining business and has the potential to be a cruise hub


* When Sri Lanka announced in July 2017 that the underperforming Chinese-built Hambantota port was to be leased for 99 years to a Chinese government-linked company, Western and Indian media outlets went into overdrive by labelling the deal a classic example of Beijing’s “debt trap”.


* The Western narrative, according to the supporters, conveniently ignores a key aspect of the deal between Sri Lanka and China.


 The transaction was not contingent on default by Sri Lanka on its external debt to China’s Exim bank; rather  it was a lease arrangement for 99 years at a fee of US$1.12 billion.


* When Hambantota was first established, its lack of proper bunkering facilities was believed to be a major drawback in attracting ships to the port.

But the recent entry of China’s oil giant Sinopec into the petroleum retail, petroleum refining and bunkering business in Sri Lanka “will be a game-changer”,  Kohona said

In November 2023, Sri Lanka’s cabinet approved Sinopec’s development of a US$4.5 billion oil refinery flanking Hambantota. When completed, the refinery will be the largest foreign direct investment ever in Sri Lanka.


* Apart from being the port of call for transshipment and oil bunkering, Hambantota also has the potential to become a cruise hub. According to Wickramasinghe, “almost all cruise vessels that call out of Colombo also call here”.

So far this year, 10 cruise ships have called at Hambantota including Serenade of the Seas, one of the world’s largest cruise ships, and those sailing from India, Thailand and the Maldives.

snippet.textDisplay:
​@yogayuliandana8958

Hambantota International Port (HIP) in Sri Lanka recorded a significant performance surge in 2025, with revenue for the first nine months estimated at over US$ 132 million. 

This revenue figure marks a 48% increase compared to the same period in 2024, driven by a 175% year-on-year increase in total cargo volumes. 

Key 2025 Performance Data (Hambantota Port):

Total Cargo Volume: 8.24 million metric tonnes (up from 3 million in 2024).

Container Throughput: Surged from 53,170 TEUs in 2024 to 428,036 TEUs in 2025.

RORO (Vehicles): 726,153 units handled (up from 579,362 in 2024).

Bulk/Breakbulk: 1.18 million metric tonnes (up 32% year-on-year).

Operational Profitability: Despite increased expenditures of ~US$ 84 million due to expansion, the port achieved higher net operating profits, largely due to increased bunkering, LPG throughput, and vehicle transshipment. 

The port's expansion continues with a US$ 41 million investment in new cranes in late 2024, increasing its annual capacity to 1 million TEUs. 

DeepSeek

@RokasStulga *China does not implement Western capitalist representative democracy. I believe many people do not understand what "socialism with Chinese characteristics" really means. Let me give you a simple example: if things were driven purely by capitalism, a significant portion of China's infrastructure would never have been completed.*

*China has many remote, high-altitude mountainous areas. According to foreign conventions, building mountain roads must be economically viable, so private enterprises are generally unwilling to build bridges and pave roads in these sparsely populated places. However, in China, such infrastructure projects are mostly undertaken by state-owned enterprises (SOEs). When SOEs establish projects or goals, they do not base their decisions on maximizing capitalist profit. That is why you will see China's high-speed railways, viaducts, winding mountain roads, and long-distance tunnels even in remote mountains and rugged terrain. These infrastructure projects are incredibly difficult to build, and some require extremely long construction cycles, but ultimately, these structures drive economic development in these regions.*

*Furthermore, regarding electricity, many people may not know that China is currently the only country in the world to achieve universal access to electricity for its 1.4 billion people. Even developed nations in Europe and America haven't achieved this, often suffering from large-scale blackouts. The greatest challenge for China in achieving universal electricity access lay in those remote corners situated among high mountains and steep ridges.*

*For instance, take Pile Village (皮勒村) in the Kashgar Prefecture of Xinjiang, located in the hinterland of the Kunlun Mountains on the Pamir Plateau. Fifteen years ago, local children had to wade through icy rivers, climb cliffs, and cross mountain ranges to get to school. Escorted by village officials, the journey of over 100 kilometers took 4 days and 3 nights on foot. In 2013, the local government completed a "Comprehensive Access Project" with a total investment of 48 million RMB, building a Class IV highway connecting Maryang Township (馬爾洋鄉) to Pile Village. The perilous journey that once took four days was transformed into a four-hour drive. Subsequently, the local government invested another 28 million RMB in a project to connect administrative villages previously reliant on photovoltaic power to the main power grid (averaging an engineering cost of about 500,000 RMB per household), ensuring that every household in Pile Village had access to electricity and the internet.*

*No matter how remote the location, the principle of the Communist Party of China is to ensure that children in mountainous areas have the right to attend school and the opportunity to access new things.*

*Another example is China's vast number of public hospitals, which ensure that medical resources do not skew solely toward the wealthy but cover the entire population of 1.4 billion. In China, seeing a doctor generally does not require waiting weeks or months for an appointment as it often does abroad; here, you can essentially be seen upon arrival, with the exception of a few specialist clinics that require appointments.*

*The West typically regards multi-party systems, representative government, and "one person, one vote" as the primary characteristics of democracy, using these as the standard to judge whether a country is democratic. China's political system does not entirely fit this definition. China emphasizes that the people are the masters of the country, adopting a system of democratic centralism that is extensive, genuine, and effective, designed to safeguard the fundamental interests of the people as a whole rather than focusing on individual, localized interests.*

snippet.textDisplay:
Much has already been demonstrated: motor control, algorithm systems, and baseline stability. It's all just a demonstration. Whether it's used for dancing or martial arts training isn't the main point. The key lies in the precision of motor control, the sufficient stability of the algorithm, and its basic balance capabilities.

There's an old Chinese saying, "To see the whole picture from a single spot," meaning to understand the underlying principles through details. Another saying is, "Laymen watch the spectacle, experts see the underlying principles." This demonstration is a great encouragement to both experts and laymen. However, industry insiders will feel not only encouraged but also despair. This is because while the technology showcased may not be a particularly advanced single technology, its integration and reliability of basic functions are disheartening.I can't think of how to compete with such an integrated company.

snippet.textDisplay: ​@BlackmythWukong_24 相信我，你所说的罗斯柴尔德家族、贝莱德、高盛、洛克菲勒家族和华尔街，这些对于中国来说，不值一提。任何一个资本利益集团都不可能是中国这样一个体量的国家实体的对手。以前的中国他们征服不了，现在的中国更无可能。中国历史上最衰败的时期，全世界都在沦为西方列强的殖民地，但同时期的中国也不过只有香港、澳门和上海、山东沿海城市划定区域的租界，而这些在新中国时期全被收回。中国几千年的大一统文明史，与任何一个西方国家的历史都不同，你们是很难理解中国这片以汉人为主体，融合多民族的土地是如何做到没有历史断层且一直延续至今，而与它同时代的文明古国至今已无一存在（埃及现在都是阿拉伯人，印度人则因沦为殖民地而与白人混杂）。有一个美国学者说过一句话：中国是一个伪装成国家的文明。它与人类历史上任何一个国家都不太相同，工业革命让西方短暂地强大不过两百多年时间，而这一短暂的技术优势，中国在1980年代开始的改革开放，只用了40年，就抹平了技术代差并完成了全工业链条的产能储备，世界上除了中国以外，没有任何一个国家能做到。去搜一下各项数据吧，说一个扎心的事实：目前中国的工业产能，有相当一部分是超越除中国以外所有国家总和的，这和二战时期德国的工业产能完全不在一个量级，德国当时只能说是出众，中国现在是“一骑绝尘”（不知道翻译能不能帮助你理解这个词汇的意思）。所以别说是美国和犹太资本，如果现在的中国真的想，一个可以打十个。只不过，自始至终被灌输儒家教育的中国人，没有西方人那样执着于扩张和占领罢了，因为我们在自己的土地上生活的已经很好了，中国搞一带一路的本质是“大家都好起来点吧，一起做生意一起赚钱，别扯我们后腿然后在那骂骂咧咧，到时候真揍你了你又要说中国欺负人。”而且中国可不是现在是这样哦？中国几千年历史上在周边地区一直扮演的是这个角色。这种心态，生活在资源贫瘠土地上所以执着于扩张的西方人是很难理解的。

The U.S. government would probably directly order U.S. troops stationed in Japan to withdraw to avoid going to war with China. At that point, whatever Japan faces would have nothing to do with the United States. Of course, political posturing would certainly continue—harsh rhetoric without real action is the way to maximize interests. snippet.textDisplay: ​@nkjono1 Accelerometers and gyros tied into a central processor for the most part. You can get a lot of processing power these days in a very small power efficient package. The programming of the movements though, that is the real magic. Movements probably recorded from motion capture of real humans, then the accelerometer and gyros tell the computer what fine balancing movement adjustments need to be made on the fly as an offset to the originally captured movement routines. There may be some external devices on set as well that help keep track of where the robots are on stage as well and in relation to people, obstacles and of course other robots. A form of GPS, cameras or light boxes as used with VR headsets like the Valve Index.
